title: Week in Orbit
summary: A mix of acquisitions and budget adjustments are stirring the pot in the space and defense sectors this week. Meanwhile, the hypersonic glide-vehicle program continues to test the limits of patience, and the commercial space landscape remains as competitive as ever.

themes.title: Acquisitions on the Rise
themes.body: Iridium's takeover of Aireon signals a strategic pivot toward enhancing aviation safety through space-based systems. Intuitive Machines' planned acquisition of a ground station company further illustrates the trend of consolidation in the industry.

themes.title: Budget Boosts Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion increase for space resilience reflects growing concerns about national security in the orbital domain. This funding could bolster efforts to counteract threats, particularly in light of recent Russian activities near commercial GEO slots.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hiccups Persist
themes.body: For the third consecutive quarter, hypersonic glide-vehicle tests have slipped, raising eyebrows about the program's trajectory. The delays may prompt a reevaluation of timelines and expectations in a field where speed is of the essence.

themes.title: Commercial Space Competition Heats Up
themes.body: With companies like True Anomaly raising significant capital and Palantir extending its ground station program, the commercial space sector is buzzing with activity. Meanwhile, AST SpaceMobile's potential use of ULA’s Vulcan rocket underscores the ongoing race to secure launch capabilities.
